AMEND (T) AND RECOMMIT TO CRIME VICTIMS, CRIME AND CORRECTION

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2072

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the correction law, in relation to authorizing any
clergy licensed by the state to visit correctional facilities

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
The purpose of this bill would include, within the provisions of
authorization, access by all licensed clergy of the state to
correctional facilities of the state. Authorization to visit
incarcerated persons is not now extended to all members of the clergy
licensed in the state; such access is limited to only those ministers
wherein the correctional facility is located.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
This bill will entitle all members of clergy licensed by or in New
York to obtain authorization to visit inmates incarcerated in state
correctional facilities.

Section 146 provides that the following persons shall be authorized to
visit at pleasure all correctional facilities: the governor and
lieutenant-governor, commissioner of general services, secretary of
state, comptroller and attorney general, members of the commission of
correction, members of the legislature, judges of the court of
appeals, supreme court and county judges, district attorneys, and
every minister of the gospel having charge of a congregation in the
town wherein any such facility is situated.

The amendment to section 146 would expand visitation eligibility and
rights of licensed clergy members and those persons incarcerated in a
state correctional facility to include visitation privileges to all
state-licensed ministry of the various religious denominations.
Provisions of this section and authorization are not applicable to any
designated areas or portions of a correctional facility in which
inmates under sentence of death are confined.

 EFFECTS OF PRESENT LAW WHICH THIS BILL WOULD ALTER :
The legislative intent of this initiative is to create the option for
persons incarcerated to receive religious services, spiritual advice,
to maintain a ministry of their faith and obtain personal counseling
from licensed clergy - other than those available virtually or merely
because of the geographical location of the correctional facility.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Persons who have been incarcerated should be allowed to participate in
and practice their known spiritual faith. Inmates should have the
option to exercise their religious beliefs and have the personal
choice of being ministered to by religious clergy from their own
community or congregation, rather than being forced or limited to
receiving spiritual advice or counseling from clergy who just happen
to reside within the boundaries of the prison. Incarcerated persons,
feeling ill at ease, are less likely to work toward recovery and
rehabilitation without the guidance of trusted and familiar
ministries. Also, if an inmate is relocated to another facility for
various reasons, this bill logically enables them to retain the
spiritual connection of members of the clergy with whom they are most
composed. Licensed members of clergy from the inmates home community
are presently excluded from offering counseling or ministerial
services merely because of geographical location. This legislative
initiative would allow licensed clergy in New York state to maintain
personal contact and continue ministerial services to members of their
faith who have unfortunately become incarcerated.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2003-04: S.644/A.1583 - Referred to Crime Victims, Crime and
Correction
2001-02: S.7749/A.11177 - Referred to Rules

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
To be determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2072A

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the correction law, in relation to persons who are
authorized to visit correctional facilities


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
Relates to authorizing ministers of congregations in the county in
which a correctional facility is located to visit inmates at pleasure.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Section 146(1) of the correction law, as amended by section 3 of part
E of chapter 56 of the laws of 2005, currently states that every
minister of the gospel having charge of a congregation in the town
wherein a jail, workhouse or correctional facility is located to visit
inmates at pleasure. The correction law will be amended by changing
town to county in relation to ministers of a congregation as defined
in section two of the religious corporations law.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Inmates who are in need of guidance from a minister of a congregation
are limited by the current law as to who they may choose to have as
their pastoral counselor because the correction law only allows those
ministers within the town where the jail, workhouse or correctional
facility is located to visit them at pleasure.  Ministers who live
within the county area have been denied access to the facilities
because the current law is not comprehensive enough.  Because there
are not enough religious persons within the town area to meet the
needs of inmates, it is necessary to expand the current law to include
the county wide area.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2007-08: A.894 - Passed Assembly; Died in Senate Crime victims, Crime
and Correction Committee 2006: A.139 Passed Assembly; died in Senate
Crime Victims, Crime and Correction 2005: A.139 - Referred to Assembly
Correction Committee 2003-04:  A.1657 - Referred to Assembly
Correction Committee

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None to state.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediate.

summary: Authorizes any clergyman of congregations in the county in which local correctional facilities are located to visit inmates; currently requires ministers to have charge of a congregation in the town in which the institution is located.
title: Authorizes any clergy licensed by the state to visit correctional facilities
